gaps.sentence: The witness claims ___ the getaway car parked outside for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'Claims to have seen' — the perfect infinitive marks an earlier action.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: He was the first climber ___ the summit without oxygen.
gaps.explanation: After 'the first/last/only + noun' a to-infinitive follows.

gaps.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.
The box was heavy enough ___ two people.
gaps.explanation: adjective + enough + to-infinitive: heavy enough to need.

gaps.sentence: Don't forget ___ the plants while we're away.
gaps.explanation: forget + to-infinitive = fail to do something you should do.
can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.
